title: DNA extraction from fungal exsiccates
author: Ursula Eberhardt
materials: Distribute tubes evenly between two 24 tube adapters of a Qiagen Tissuelyzer and disrupt material at maximum speed for three minutes. Extend disruption time if needed.

steps.title: Prepare tubes and steel bead
steps.instruction: For each sample, label a 1.5 ml safe‑lock centrifuge tube, place a 2 mm steel bead inside, and optionally set aside a second 1.5 ml safe‑lock tube containing 300 µl isopropanol (to be used later).

steps.title: Add fungal tissue
steps.instruction: Using clean tools, transfer a small crumb of fungal exsiccate (visible dot up to 1–2 mm lamellae) into the tube.

steps.title: Add Cell Lysis Solution
steps.instruction: Add 300 µl Cell Lysis Solution to each tube, opening only one tube at a time; turn the tube upside down to suspend any powder on the lid, then vortex to disperse the powder in the liquid.

steps.title: Incubate old material (optional)
steps.instruction: For old or scarce material, incubate the tube overnight at 37 °C with minimum shaking, and mix by inverting periodically.

steps.title: Cool to room temperature
steps.instruction: Cool the tubes to room temperature, e.g., by placing them in a freezer for a few minutes.

steps.title: Add Protein Precipitation Solution
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl Protein Precipitation Solution, then mix by inverting 150 times or vortex briefly (up to 96 tubes can be inverted simultaneously using a duplicate rack).

steps.title: Room‑temperature incubation
steps.instruction: Leave the tubes at room temperature for at least 15 min; the liquid often becomes milky.

steps.title: Heat incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate at 65 °C for 1 h with minimum shaking; for young, abundant material the incubation may be reduced to 15 min.

steps.title: Add DNA hydration solution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl DNA hydration solution to each tube and mix.

steps.title: Prepare isopropanol capture tube
steps.instruction: Prepare a clean 1.5 ml safe‑lock tube containing 300 µl isopropanol; for old or scarce material add 1 µl glycogen solution (1:1 diluted with ultrapure water) into the tube lid.

steps.title: Centrifuge first spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for at least 5 min, then proceed immediately to the next step.

steps.title: Transfer to isopropanol
steps.instruction: Pour each lysate into its prepared isopropanol tube; if the steel bead accidentally transfers, remove it with a stirring magnet slid along the tube exterior and discard the bead. The pelleted fungal fragments may be discarded or retained for a second extraction.

steps.title: Mix isopropanol suspension
steps.instruction: Mix by inverting 150 times or vortexing.

steps.title: Centrifuge second spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for at least 5 min and proceed immediately.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and drain
steps.instruction: Pour off the supernatant, place the tube upside down on a prepared tissue to let remaining liquid trickle down; the pellet is often visible. Leave for a few minutes before blotting and turning the tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge third spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for at least 5 min and proceed immediately.

steps.title: Ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 300 µl high‑quality 70 % ethanol (non‑degenerated), mix by inverting or vortexing.

steps.title: Remove ethanol and dry
steps.instruction: Pour off the ethanol, place the tube upside down on tissue to drain, and let stand for no more than 10 min before the next step.

steps.title: Final drying
steps.instruction: Place tubes at 65 °C for 1 h with optional gentle shaking.

steps.title: Post‑extraction handling
steps.instruction: Leave extracts overnight at room temperature (or in the fridge for old/scarce material); thereafter store at –20 °C or –80 °C for long‑term. For PCR, dilute extracts 1:25–1:50 for ribosomal genes or 1:25 for single‑copy genes (e.g., 1 µl DNA + 49 µl ultrapure water, use 2.5 µl of this dilution in a 25 µl PCR). If PCR fails, try higher concentrations. Use multichannel pipettors for dilutions in strips or 96‑well plates.
